lessons.title: if, else and comparisons
lessons.summary: Making a program choose between two paths.
lessons.notes:
**Selection** means the program picks which lines to run.

```python
if age >= 18:
    print("Adult")
else:
    print("Child")
```

Comparison operators: `==` equal to, `!=` not equal to, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`.

---

Two classic mistakes:
- using `=` (assignment) when you mean `==` (comparison)
- forgetting the colon or the indentation under the `if`
lessons.worked_example_note: Only one of the two `print` lines can ever run. The indented block belongs to the branch above it.

lessons.title: If, else and comparisons: more practice
lessons.summary: More practice with the basics before moving on to elif chains.
lessons.notes:
Before adding more branches, it's worth being completely comfortable with a single `if` / `else` and the six comparison operators: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`.

Remember the two classic mistakes from the last lesson: `=` instead of `==`, and a missing colon or indentation.

A condition can compare numbers, or compare text with `==` — but text comparisons are **case sensitive**, so `"Yes"` and `"yes"` are not equal.
lessons.worked_example_note: % gives the remainder after dividing by 2 — a remainder of 0 means the number divides evenly.

lessons.title: elif chains and logical operators
lessons.summary: More than two options, and conditions joined with and/or/not.
lessons.notes:
Use `elif` for a chain of options. Python checks them in order and stops at the first one that is true, so **order matters** — put the strictest boundary first.

```python
if mark >= 80:
    grade = "9"
elif mark >= 60:
    grade = "7"
else:
    grade = "4"
```

---

Join conditions with `and` (both must be true), `or` (at least one), `not` (reverses it).

OCR wording tip: *"between 10 and 20 inclusive"* becomes `if 10 <= n <= 20:` or `if n >= 10 and n <= 20:`.
lessons.worked_example_note: `and` needs both sides to be true. Compare strings with `==` and remember they are case sensitive.

lessons.title: Exam-style selection problems
lessons.summary: Working out the boundaries from a written scenario.
lessons.notes:
Exam scenarios hide the conditions inside sentences. Build a small table before you code:

```text
Condition          Output
90 or more         Gold
70 to 89           Silver
less than 70       Bronze
```

---

Then write one branch per row, strictest first. Check the **boundary values** (exactly 90, exactly 70) — that is where marks are usually lost.
lessons.worked_example:
# Discount: 10% off orders of 50 or more, 5% off orders of 20 or more
total = float(input())
if total >= 50:
    total = total * 0.9
elif total >= 20:
    total = total * 0.95
print(round(total, 2))
lessons.worked_example_note: There is no `else` here because orders under £20 need no change at all.

quiz.question: Which operator checks if two values are equal in Python?
quiz.explanation: = assigns a value; == compares two values for equality.

quiz.question: In if age >= 18: print("Adult") else: print("Child"), what happens when age is exactly 18?
quiz.explanation: >= includes the boundary value itself, so 18 counts as "18 or more".

quiz.question: What's wrong with if age = 18:?
options: = is assignment, not comparison — it should be ==
quiz.answer: = is assignment, not comparison — it should be ==
quiz.explanation: Using = instead of == is one of the two classic if-statement mistakes.

quiz.question: Are "Yes" and "yes" equal when compared with ==?
options: No — text comparison is case sensitive
quiz.answer: No — text comparison is case sensitive
quiz.explanation: Python compares text exactly as written, so a different capital letter makes two strings unequal.

quiz.question: In if a > b: ... elif a < b: ... else: ..., when does the else branch run?
options: When a and b are equal
quiz.answer: When a and b are equal
quiz.explanation: The else only runs once both the > and < checks above it have failed, which leaves equality as the only case left.

quiz.question: In an elif chain, what happens once Python finds a true condition?
options: It runs that branch and skips the rest of the chain
It checks every remaining condition anyway
quiz.answer: It runs that branch and skips the rest of the chain
quiz.explanation: Python checks elif conditions in order and stops at the first true one — this is why order matters.

quiz.question: Why does order matter in an elif chain checking exam grade boundaries?
options: Because the first true condition wins, so stricter boundaries must come first
It doesn't matter what order they're in
Because elif only works with 2 branches
quiz.answer: Because the first true condition wins, so stricter boundaries must come first

quiz.question: Which operator requires both conditions to be true?
quiz.explanation: and only lets the combined condition through if both sides are true; or only needs one.

quiz.question: Where are marks usually lost in boundary-based selection questions?
options: At the exact boundary values, like exactly 90 or exactly 70
At the very start of the program
quiz.answer: At the exact boundary values, like exactly 90 or exactly 70

quiz.question: Before coding a scenario with multiple bands (like Gold/Silver/Bronze), what should you do first?
options: Build a small table of conditions and their outputs
Guess which band is most common
quiz.answer: Build a small table of conditions and their outputs

quiz.question: In an elif chain for grade bands, which boundary should usually be checked first?
quiz.explanation: Since the first true condition wins, checking the highest band first stops higher scorers being wrongly caught by a lower band's condition.

tasks.title: Positive or negative
tasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Positive` if it is greater than 0. Otherwise print `Not positive`.
hints: Exactly one of the two branches runs — decide the condition first, then fill in what each branch prints.
The pattern is `if <condition>: ... else: ...` — work out what the condition should compare first.

tasks.title: Old enough to vote
tasks.brief: Input an age. Print `Can vote` if the age is 18 or more. Otherwise print `Too young`.
hints: "18 or more" includes exactly 18, so use >= rather than >.
Use `>=` rather than `>` whenever the boundary value itself should count as meeting the rule.

tasks.title: Bigger of two
tasks.brief: Input two whole numbers, one per line. Print the larger one. If they are equal, print `Equal` instead.
hints: There are three possible outcomes here, not two — you need a third branch for the equal case.
Three outcomes need an `if / elif / else` chain, not just `if / else` — compare the two values in each branch.

tasks.title: Largest of three
tasks.brief:
Read three whole numbers, one per line. Print the largest of the three. If two or more of them are tied for the largest, print `Tie` instead.

For example, 3, 9 and 5 prints 9. 7, 7 and 2 prints Tie.
hints: Python's built-in max() finds the largest of several values for you. Think about what it would mean if more than one value matched that largest value.
Once you know the largest value, compare each of the original values against it to work out how many match.

tasks.title: Even or odd
tasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Even` if it divides evenly by 2. Otherwise print `Odd`.
hints: % gives the remainder after dividing by 2 — zero means it divides evenly.
The pattern is `if n % 2 == 0: ... else: ...`.

tasks.title: Enough money
tasks.brief: Input the price of an item, then how much money you have, one per line. Print `Can afford` if you have enough money to buy it. Otherwise print `Not enough`.
hints: "Enough" includes having exactly the price, so use >= rather than >.
The pattern is `if money >= price: ... else: ...`.

tasks.title: Warmer, cooler or the same
tasks.brief: Input today's temperature, then yesterday's temperature, one per line. Print `Warmer` if today is higher, `Cooler` if today is lower, or `Same` if they are equal.
hints: There are three possible outcomes here, not two, so you need a third branch.
The pattern is `if today > yesterday: ... elif today < yesterday: ... else: ...`.

tasks.title: Correct password
tasks.brief: Input a password. Print `Correct` if it exactly matches `python123`. Otherwise print `Incorrect`.
hints: String comparisons are case sensitive — check the exact spelling given.
The pattern is `if password == "python123": ... else: ...`.

tasks.title: Closest to the target
tasks.brief:
Input a target number, then two other numbers, one per line. Print whichever of the two numbers is closer to the target. If they are equally close, print `Tie` instead.

For example, target 10 with 7 and 12 prints 12 (it's 2 away, versus 3 away for 7).
hints: Work out how far each number is from the target first — a negative difference is just as far away as a positive one.
Compare the two distances from the target, using abs() to ignore whether each difference is positive or negative.

tasks.title: Traffic light
tasks.brief: Input the colour of a traffic light. Print `Stop` for `red`, `Get ready` for `amber` and `Go` for `green`. For anything else, print `Broken`.
hints: You have four possible outputs, so you need an if / elif / elif / else chain, not just if / else.
String comparisons are case sensitive — "red" and "Red" are not equal

tasks.title: In range
tasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `In range` if it is between 10 and 20 inclusive — meaning 10 and 20 themselves both count as in range. Otherwise print `Out of range`.
hints: Python lets you chain two comparisons in one condition to check a value falls between two boundaries, inclusive on both ends.
The pattern is `if lower <= value <= upper: ... else: ...`, using the boundaries given in the brief.

tasks.title: Login with two checks
tasks.brief: Input a username, then a password, one per line. Print `Welcome` only if the username is exactly `admin` and the password is exactly `hcode`. Otherwise print `Rejected`.
hints: Both checks must be true at once, so join the two conditions with and.
The pattern is `if <condition1> and <condition2>: ... else: ...` — both sides must be true.

tasks.title: VIP eligibility
tasks.brief:
A loyalty scheme grants VIP status under either of two rules:

- the customer is 18 or older AND has been a member for at least 2 years, OR
- the customer has been a member for at least 5 years, whatever their age

Read the customer's age, then the number of years they've been a member, one per line. Print `VIP` if either rule applies, otherwise print `Not VIP`.

For example, age 20 with 3 years membership is VIP (meets the first rule). Age 16 with 6 years membership is also VIP (meets the second rule — age doesn't matter there).
hints: Write the two rules as two separate conditions first, then think about how to combine them so meeting either one is enough.
Join the two separate conditions with `or` inside a single if statement — brackets around each combined part can help keep it readable.

tasks.title: Swimming pool entry
tasks.brief:
A swimming pool charges different prices by age:

- under 5: free
- 5 to 15: £2
- 16 to 64 (adult): £4
- 65 or over: £2

Read a person's age. Display the price they pay, as a whole number of pounds.

For example, age 30 pays £4, so print `4`.
hints: Build the branches in age order, from youngest to oldest, checking the strictest boundary first. There are four price groups, not two, so you'll need an elif chain.
The pattern is `if age < a: ... elif age < b: ... elif age < c: ... else: ...` — two branches can end up giving the same price, they're just different age groups.

tasks.title: Parcel size checker
tasks.brief:
A courier classifies parcels by weight in kilograms:

- up to and including 2 kg: `Small`
- over 2 kg, up to and including 10 kg: `Medium`
- over 10 kg, up to and including 30 kg: `Large`
- over 30 kg: `Refused`

Read the weight as a decimal. Display the classification.
hints: Check the Refused case and the Large case before the smaller ones, so the boundaries at exactly 2, 10 and 30 land in the right group.
The pattern is `if weight > biggest: ... elif weight > next: ... else: ...` — checking from the largest boundary down avoids overlap.

tasks.title: Quiz feedback
tasks.brief:
A quiz is marked out of 20:

- 18 or more: `Excellent`
- 14 to 17: `Good`
- 10 to 13: `Pass`
- below 10: `Revise this topic`

A mark outside the range 0 to 20 is invalid and should display `Invalid mark` instead of any of the above.

Read the mark scored. Display the appropriate result.
hints: Check whether the mark is invalid (below 0 or above 20) before checking any of the grade boundaries.
Order the grade boundaries from highest down, same pattern as the lesson's elif example

tasks.title: Theme park ride restrictions
tasks.brief:
A theme park needs software to check whether a visitor may ride a rollercoaster.

- A visitor may ride if they are at least 140 cm tall AND aged 12 or over.
- A visitor who is tall enough (140 cm or more) but under 12 may still ride if an adult is with them.
- Anyone under 140 cm may never ride, whatever their age or whether an adult is with them.

Read three lines of input: height in centimetres (whole number), age (whole number), then `yes` or `no` for whether an adult is with them.

Output exactly one of:
- `Ride allowed`
- `Ride allowed with adult`
- `Ride refused`
hints: Deal with the height rule first — anyone under 140 cm is refused no matter what the other answers are.
Then, among those tall enough, split on age, then on the adult answer

tasks.title: Broadband billing
tasks.brief:
An internet provider bills customers monthly:

- The standard package costs £25 per month and includes 100 GB of data.
- Data used above the 100 GB allowance costs £1.50 per whole gigabyte over the limit.
- Customers who have been with the provider for 24 months or more get a 10% discount on the whole bill, applied after any excess data charge has been added.

Read the gigabytes used (a whole number), then the number of months the customer has been with the provider (a whole number). Output the final bill, rounded to 2 decimal places, in the format `Bill: £<amount>`.

For example, 80 GB used over 5 months (no excess, no discount) gives `Bill: £25.0`.
hints: Excess data only applies when usage is above 100 — work that out first and add it to the base £25.
Apply the loyalty discount last, to the total bill so far, not just to the excess charge

tasks.title: Library fine system
tasks.brief:
A school library charges fines for late books:

- returned up to 3 days late: no fine
- from day 4 onwards: 20p per day late, counting all the days late, not just the days after day 3
- the fine is capped at £5.00, however late the book is
- students in Year 7 are never fined, whatever the rules above say

Read the number of days late (a whole number), then the student's year group (a whole number). Output the fine, in pounds, to 2 decimal places, in the format `Fine: £<amount>`.
hints: Check the Year 7 rule first — it overrides every other rule, so it should be the very first thing you check.
Work out the uncapped fine first, then use a second if statement to bring it down to the stated maximum if it's gone over.

tasks.title: Exam retake eligibility
tasks.brief:
An exam board decides whether a student may retake an exam:

- if the mark is 40 or above, the student has passed and does not need a retake, however many attempts they've had
- if the mark is below 40, the student may retake the exam if they have had fewer than 3 previous attempts
- if the mark is below 40 and they have already had 3 or more attempts, no more retakes are allowed

Read the mark (whole number), then the number of previous attempts (whole number). Print exactly one of `Passed`, `Retake allowed` or `No more attempts`.
hints: Check the pass condition first — if it's true, the number of attempts doesn't matter at all, so nothing else needs checking.
The pattern is `if <pass condition>: ... elif <retake condition>: ... else: ...` — order matters here.

homeworkTasks.title: Even or odd
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Even` if it divides evenly by 2, otherwise print `Odd`.
hints: % gives the remainder after division — zero means it divides evenly.
The pattern is `if n % 2 == 0: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Positive, negative or zero
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Positive` if it's greater than 0, `Negative` if it's less than 0, or `Zero` if it's exactly 0.
hints: There are three outcomes, so you need an if / elif / else chain, not just if / else.
Check greater than 0 first, then less than 0, with else catching exactly 0.

homeworkTasks.title: Pass or fail
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number mark out of 100. Print `Pass` if it's 50 or above, otherwise print `Fail`.
hints: "50 or above" includes exactly 50, so use >= rather than >.
The pattern is `if mark >= 50: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Speeding check
homeworkTasks.brief: The speed limit is 70. Input a whole number speed. Print `Ticket` if the speed is over 70, otherwise print `OK`.
hints: "Over" the limit means strictly greater than, not equal to.
The pattern is `if speed > 70: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Member discount
homeworkTasks.brief: A shop gives a discount to members who spend £50 or more. Input whether the customer is a member (yes or no). Input how much they spent, which may include pence. Print `Discount` if they are a member and spent at least £50, otherwise print `No discount`.
hints: Both conditions must be true at once, so join them with and.
The pattern is `if is_member == "yes" and spent >= 50: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Free shipping
homeworkTasks.brief: An online shop gives free shipping if a customer spends £30 or more, or if they are already a member. Input how much they spent (may include pence). Input whether they are a member (yes or no). Print `Free shipping` if either condition is true, otherwise print `Shipping charged`.
hints: Only one of the two conditions needs to be true, so join them with or.
The pattern is `if spent >= 30 or is_member == "yes": ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Weather advice
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number temperature in °C. Print `Freezing` if it's below 0, `Cold` if it's below 15, `Mild` if it's below 25, or `Hot` otherwise.
hints: Check the boundaries in order from lowest to highest, so each elif only needs to handle what the earlier checks ruled out.
The pattern is `if temp < 0: ... elif temp < 15: ... elif temp < 25: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: In range 1 to 10
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `In range` if it's between 1 and 10 inclusive, otherwise print `Out of range`.
hints: Python lets you chain two comparisons in one condition to check a value falls between two boundaries.
The pattern is `if 1 <= n <= 10: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Password length check
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a password. Print `Valid` if it's at least 8 characters long, otherwise print `Too short`.
hints: len() gives the number of characters in a string.
The pattern is `if len(password) >= 8: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Leap year check
homeworkTasks.brief: A year is a leap year if it divides evenly by 4, unless it also divides evenly by 100 — in which case it's only a leap year if it also divides evenly by 400. Input a whole number year. Print `Leap year` or `Not a leap year`.
hints: Combine and/or carefully: divides by 4 AND (doesn't divide by 100 OR does divide by 400).
The full condition can be built and stored in one Boolean variable before the if statement, to keep it readable.

homeworkTasks.title: Grade classification
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number percentage. Print `Distinction` for 90 or above, `Merit` for 70 or above, `Pass` for 40 or above, or `Fail` otherwise.
hints: Check the highest boundary first, then work downward.
The pattern is `if pct >= 90: ... elif pct >= 70: ... elif pct >= 40: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Ticket age category
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number age. Print `Child` if under 12, `Senior` if 65 or over, or `Adult` otherwise.
hints: Check the child boundary first, then the senior boundary, with else covering everyone left.
The pattern is `if age < 12: ... elif age >= 65: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Two-factor check
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a 4-digit code. Input whether the device is trusted (yes or no). Print `Access granted` only if the code is exactly 1234 and the device is trusted, otherwise print `Access denied`.
hints: Both checks must be true at once, so join them with and.
The pattern is `if code == "1234" and device == "yes": ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Simple calculator
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a mathematical operator, which will be one of +, - or *. Input two whole numbers, one at a time. Print the result of applying that operator to the two numbers, in that order.
hints: Three possible operators means an if / elif / elif chain, comparing the operator string in each branch.
The pattern is `if op == "+": ... elif op == "-": ... elif op == "*": ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Store open check
homeworkTasks.brief: A store is open from 9 (inclusive) until 18 (exclusive), on a 24-hour clock. Input a whole number hour. Print `Open` if the store is open at that hour, otherwise print `Closed`.
hints: Both boundaries must hold at once, so join them with and.
The pattern is `if hour >= 9 and hour < 18: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Ice warning
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number temperature in °C. Print `Ice warning` if it's 0 or below, otherwise print `Safe`.
hints: "0 or below" includes exactly 0, so use <= rather than <.
The pattern is `if temp <= 0: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Speed category
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number speed. Print `Slow` for under 30, `Medium` for under 60, or `Fast` otherwise.
hints: Check the lowest boundary first, then the next.
The pattern is `if speed < 30: ... elif speed < 60: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Discount code
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a discount code. Print `Applied` if it exactly matches SAVE10, otherwise print `Invalid code`.
hints: String comparisons are case sensitive — check the exact spelling given.
The pattern is `if code == "SAVE10": ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Multiple of 3 and 5
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Both` if it divides evenly by both 3 and 5, otherwise print `No`.
hints: Two separate % checks, joined with and.
The pattern is `if n % 3 == 0 and n % 5 == 0: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Refund eligibility
homeworkTasks.brief: Input how many days before an event a ticket is being returned, a whole number. Print `Full refund` for 7 or more days, `Partial refund` for 2 or more days, or `No refund` otherwise.
hints: Check the largest boundary first, then work downward.
The pattern is `if days >= 7: ... elif days >= 2: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Membership tier
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number of loyalty points. Print `Gold` for 1000 or more, `Silver` for 500 or more, `Bronze` for 100 or more, or `None` otherwise.
hints: Check the highest boundary first, then work downward through the rest.
The pattern is `if points >= 1000: ... elif points >= 500: ... elif points >= 100: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Certificate eligibility
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number mark and a whole number attendance percentage. Print `Certificate` if the mark is 40 or above and attendance is 80 or above, otherwise print `No certificate`.
hints: Both conditions must hold at once, so join them with and.
The pattern is `if mark >= 40 and attendance >= 80: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Age category
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number age. Print `Child` for under 13, `Teen` for under 20, or `Adult` otherwise.
hints: Check the lowest boundary first, then the next.
The pattern is `if age < 13: ... elif age < 20: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Positive even check
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Positive even` if it's greater than 0 and divides evenly by 2, otherwise print `Other`.
hints: Both conditions must hold at once, so join them with and.
The pattern is `if n > 0 and n % 2 == 0: ... else: ...`.

homeworkTasks.title: Exam entry check
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number age. Input whether coursework has been submitted (yes or no). Print `Entered` if the student is at least 16 and has submitted coursework, otherwise print `Not entered`.
hints: Both conditions must hold at once, so join them with and.
The pattern is `if age >= 16 and coursework == "yes": ... else: ...`.

projectTasks.title: Parcel delivery estimator — Part A: heavy or standard
projectTasks.brief:
A courier is building a delivery cost estimator, split into three parts — each part builds directly on the code you write for the one before it, so keep what you've written rather than starting over.

**Part A.** Read a parcel's weight in kg, which may include decimals. Print `Heavy parcel` if it weighs more than 5kg, otherwise print `Standard parcel`.
hints: Compare the weight to 5 using an if/else.
Cast the input to a float, then check if it's greater than 5 before printing the matching message.

projectTasks.title: Parcel delivery estimator — Part B: the cost
projectTasks.brief: **Part B.** Your code carries on from Part A — keep everything you already wrote and add to it. Standard parcels (5kg or under) cost a flat £3.50. Heavy parcels cost £3.50 plus £1.20 for every kg over 5. No new input needed — reuse the weight you already read. After your Part A message, print the delivery cost, rounded to 2 decimal places, as a new line in the format `Cost: £<amount>`.
hints: Don't delete your Part A code — reuse the weight variable you already have, then add a new print statement.
if weight > 5: cost = round(3.50 + 1.20 * (weight - 5), 2) else: cost = 3.50 — then print it, added after your existing Part A message.

projectTasks.title: Parcel delivery estimator — Part C: next-day surcharge
projectTasks.brief: **Part C.** Keep everything from Parts A and B. Also read whether next-day delivery is wanted (`yes` or `no`). After your Part B lines, print the final cost (the cost you already calculated, plus a flat £4.00 surcharge if next-day delivery was chosen), rounded to 2 decimal places, as a new line in the format `Total: £<amount>`.
hints: Reuse the cost variable from Part B rather than recalculating it from scratch.
nextday = input(); total = round(cost + 4.00, 2) if nextday == "yes" else cost — then print it, added after your existing lines.

practiceTasks.title: Voting age checker
practiceTasks.brief: Input a person's age. Print `Can vote` if they are 18 or over, otherwise print `Cannot vote`.
hints: Compare the age to 18 with >=.
if age >= 18: print("Can vote") else: print("Cannot vote").

practiceTasks.title: Positive or negative
practiceTasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Positive` if it's greater than 0, `Negative` if it's less than 0, or `Zero` if it's exactly 0.
hints: Three possible outcomes needs an if / elif / else chain.
if n > 0: ... elif n < 0: ... else: print("Zero").

practiceTasks.title: Speed camera
practiceTasks.brief: A road has a 30mph speed limit. Input a car's speed. Print `Speeding` if it's over 30, otherwise print `Within limit`.
hints: Compare the speed to 30 with >.
if speed > 30: print("Speeding") else: print("Within limit").

practiceTasks.title: Cinema age rating
practiceTasks.brief: A cinema uses age ratings U, 12, 15 and 18. Input a person's age. Print the highest rating they're allowed to watch: `18` for 18 or over, `15` for 15 or over, `12` for 12 or over, otherwise `U`.
hints: Check the highest boundary first in an elif chain, so a 20-year-old doesn't also match the 12+ or 15+ checks.
if age >= 18: ... elif age >= 15: ... elif age >= 12: ... else: print("U").

practiceTasks.title: Data allowance
practiceTasks.brief: A phone plan includes 500MB of data. Input how many MB have been used. If it's over 500, print how many MB over in the format `Over allowance: <n>MB`; otherwise print how many MB are left, in the format `Remaining: <n>MB`.
hints: Compare the used amount to 500, then work out the difference either way round.
if used > 500: print(f"Over allowance: {used - 500}MB") else: print(f"Remaining: {500 - used}MB").

practiceTasks.title: Grade classifier
practiceTasks.brief: Input a score out of 100, a whole number. Print `Pass` if it's 40 or above, otherwise print `Fail`.
hints: A single if/else compares the score to 40.
if score >= 40: print("Pass") else: print("Fail").

practiceTasks.title: Even, odd or zero
practiceTasks.brief: Input a whole number. Print `Zero` if it's 0, `Even` if it's even, or `Odd` if it's odd.
hints: Check for 0 first, then use % 2 to tell even from odd for everything else.
if n == 0: print("Zero") elif n % 2 == 0: print("Even") else: print("Odd").

practiceTasks.title: Triangle classifier
practiceTasks.brief: Input three side lengths of a triangle, one at a time, whole numbers. If the two shortest sides don't add up to more than the longest, the shape isn't a valid triangle at all — print `Not a triangle`. Otherwise, print `Equilateral` if all three sides are equal, `Isosceles` if exactly two are equal, or `Scalene` if all three are different.
hints: Sort the three sides first so you always know which is longest, then check the triangle rule before checking for equal sides.
sides = sorted([a, b, c]); if sides[0] + sides[1] <= sides[2]: print("Not a triangle") — otherwise compare a, b and c for equality to decide between the other three.

practiceTasks.title: Loyalty discount tier
